This program is intended to meet the spirit and intent of the following regulations:
California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2
Federal EPA Risk Management Program (RMP)  Title 40 CFR §68
California Process Safety Management (PSM) Program  Title 8 CCR §5189
Federal Process Safety Management (PSM) Program  Title 29 CFR §1910.119

Hereafter this program will be referred to as the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program.

This program is intended to be a living document. As such, the information, procedures, policies, and documentation that make up this program must be made easily accessible and updated as necessary. To accomplish this, the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has elected to use PSMWriter, software developed and distributed by Resource Compliance, Inc. This software will assist us with updating, maintaining, scheduling, and tracking RMP/PSM/CalARP related activities. 

1.1 City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant, Risk and Process Safety Management Program

This is to inform all interested persons, including employees, that the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has developed their unified RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. This program has been prepared to address the risks involved in operating and maintaining the following processes which have the presence of hazardous chemicals above threshold quantities: 

Process Name                                            |  Process Chemical                               | Process Quantity
Chlorine                                                           Chlorine                                                     8,000 lbs

Our RMP/PSM/CalARP Program promotes overall plant, worker, public, and environmental safety. The program enables our facility to prevent the occurrence, and minimize the consequences, of significant releases of hazardous chemicals. Overall, the program is designed to prevent accidental fatalities, injuries, illnesses, and physical property damage.

r company has many policies and procedures in place to promote overall plant, worker and public safety. We have: 
Prepared a unified program based on the PSM regulation to meet CalARP and RMP obligations as well
Organized the program so that it meshes closely with general business practices
Utilized PSMWriter software to ensure that all necessary employees have access to relevant information (SOPs, PHAs, audits, etc.)

The RMP/PSM/CalARP Program sets forth rules, procedures, and practices that will help our employees and neighbors protect themselves.

1.2 Process Descriptions

Chlorine
The process operates as follows: two (2) ton containers are connected to the water treatment process through process tubing and piping. Chlorine gas is withdrawn from the ton containers by vacuum. This vacuum opens the vacuum regulator diaphragm and withdraws the chlorine gas from the ton containers at a controlled feed rate set by the operators with the use of the chlorine feed regulator and rotameter mounted to the wall. The gas is injected into the feed water line where it becomes a chlorine/water solution and is distributed to the location where it is needed in the treatment process. The analyzers monitor chlorine concentrations in the water and relay the information to the chlorine feed regulator in order to determine whether more or less chlorine should be injected.

1.3 General Accident Release & Chemical Specific Prevention Steps

1.3.1 General 

We inform our employees engaged in process operations of the dangers of an accidental release of aqueous ammonia and chlorine in annual safety meetings. During these meetings we also discuss preventative measures, such as evacuation, in order to be prepared for a release.
The City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has also conducted an off-site consequence analysis of worst-case and alternative release scenarios for the aqueous ammonia and chlorine process. These are for the purposes of informing the public in the event of an acciden

tal release. The results of the analyses are reported in PSMWriter and hard copy binders.

1.3.3 Chlorine
The chlorination process at the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant facility is an integral part of the overall business and operates for only a few months out of the year. As with the ammonia process management is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of a chlorine leak. 

City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant personnel monitor the chlorination process. In addition, the process is checked frequently during the operational season by our outside water treatment contractor. This contractor also assists in performing the annual mechanical integrity review of our chlorine equipment. 

1.4 Five Year Accident History

The City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has had no accidental release within the last five (5) years.

1.5 Emergency Action and Response Plan

The City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plants emergency action and response program has been developed to satisfy the following requirements:
Cal/OSHAs Emergency Action Plan  Title 8 CCR §3220
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Emergency Action Plans  Title 29 CFR §1910.38
Cal/OSHAs Process Safety Management [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 8 CCR §5189(n)
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Process Safety Management [Emergency Planning and Response Requirements]  Title 29 CFR §1910.119(n)
California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2 §5120.1-5120.2
USEPA Risk Management Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 40 CFR §68.90-96
California Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) [Emergency Response Plans and Procedures]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 1 §5030.7

Strategically, the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has chosen to be a non-responding stationary source. Our employee

s will not respond to accidental releases of aqueous ammonia and chlorine. In lieu of responding to accidental releases, the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant is implementing the following protocols:
The facility is included in the community emergency response plan developed under Title 42 USC §11003.
Appropriate mechanisms are in place to notify emergency responders when there is a need for a response.
Annual emergency response coordination activities are performed (Section 1.5.1).
Annual notification exercises are performed (Section 1.5.2).

1.5.1 Emergency Response Coordination Activities

The purpose of emergency response coordination activities is to coordinate response needs with local emergency planning and response organizations. The intent is for local response organizations to be made aware of the regulated substances at the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant, their quantities, the risks presented by the covered processes, and the resources and capabilities at our facility to respond to an accidental release of a regulated substance. The emergency response coordination activities will consist of the following:
Coordinations will be completed at least annually. Additional coordinations will be made to account for changes at our facility that may affect the community emergency response plan.
Coordinations will include the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plants emergency response plan, updated emergency contact information, and any other information necessary for developing and implementing the local emergency response plan.

Coordination activities will be appropriately documented. The coordination records will include the names of individuals involved and their contact information (phone number, email address, and organizational affiliations), dates of coordination activities, and nature of coordination activities.
The disclosure of information classified or restricted by the Department of Defense or other Federal agencies or contractors of su

ch agencies is controlled by applicable laws, regulations, or executive orders concerning the release of that classified or restricted information.
1.5.2 Emergency Response Notification Exercises
At least once per calendar year, the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant will conduct an exercise of the facilitys emergency response notifications mechanism. The facility will record each notification exercise utilizing PSMWriter.

Alternatively, the facility may meet the notification requirements through other exercises conducted to meet other Federal, state or local requirements, provided that the necessary notification is performed. Additionally, if a notification is made in response to an accidental release, this would also satisfy the notification requirement.

1.6 Planned Changes to Improve Safety

The City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has implemented many policies and procedures to promote overall plant, worker, public, and environmental safety. Nevertheless, the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant continually strives to improve in all areas, including safety.
By utilizing PSMWriter software, all necessary employees have access to every aspect of the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. This has improved the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plants ability to communicate hazardous situations to employees and contractors. In addition, PSMWriter tracks all RMP/PSM/CalARP related events so that the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plants management team can ensure that the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program is being implemented.
The City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has implemented all aspects of the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program. When a RMP/PSM/CalARP Program requirement is completed (i.e. mechanical integrity inspection, process hazard analysis, compliance audit, etc.) any specific action items related to that event are entered into PSMWriter, assigned a responsible person, and given a due date. Once the action item has been completed, the resolution can be documented using

PSMWriter as well. A list of current or past due action items can be accessed at any time by those with access to PSMWriter.

In addition to utilizing PSMWriter to create, schedule, track, and document events, the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant has also entered into a contract with Resource Compliance to obtain help with RMP/PSM/CalARP Program implementation.

The City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant considers the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program a living document. It is an interactive framework that guides safe action for the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant employees, but allows for feedback and continual improvement. Through the RMP/PSM/CalARP Program the City of Coalinga Water Filtration Plant will continue to maintain overall plant worker, public, and environmental safety.
